rationale: This contact sheet shows only 2 visible candidates, both within the same stepped prismatic family. The portfolio therefore fails the 20-option standard immediately: far too few candidates are visible, the dominant family share is effectively 100%, and the two options repeat the same footprint/roof logic with only minor split/notch variation. For the given neighborhood-life brief, the set also lacks enough program-specific spatial differentiation: no clearly distinct courtyard/cut/terrace system is yet demonstrated, and the upper massing reads as one repeated boxy-stacked chassis rather than a range of access-bound street-building relations. Both candidates should be replaced or heavily reworked into different spatial families while preserving active ground edge and a legible public void/terrace.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: small compact prismatic stepped mass with entry notch / split-step variation; same active-edge logic, same stepped roof, same box-bar chassis family

required_next_relations: Introduce at least 10 materially different mass families across the 20-option set, not just label changes.

Keep the active ground edge, but vary the access-bound relation through courtyard, carve_void, notch, setback, terrace, cantilever, bridge, cross_mass, bent_bar, split_wing, attach_volume, lift, puncture, cut_corner, or stepped_mass.
Ensure one clearly legible public void or terrace that supports mixed-use ground life rather than decorative subtraction.
Separate upper mass from ground mass so the calm upper hierarchy remains readable without repeating the same stepped roof chassis.
Avoid repeating the same footprint or roof silhouette more than once; diversify section language as much as plan language.
Aim for street-building typologies: retail/cafe/community/mixed-use fronts with distinct threshold conditions and varied upper consolidation.
